title: Dattopant Thengadi National Board for Workers' Education and Development
author: Editorial Desk
summary: The Central Board for Workers' Education carries the founder's name.
body:
The **Central Board for Workers' Education (CBWE)** was set up in 1958 under the Ministry of Labour and Employment. Its work is to educate workers, to make them aware of their rights and duties, and to train worker-teachers who run classes in their own workplaces and communities.

## A new name

The Board now carries the name **Dattopant Thengadi National Board for Workers' Education and Development (DTNBWED)**. The name honours the founder of BMS, whose life was devoted to teaching workers as organisers and as citizens.

## What it does

- Trains **worker-teachers** and **educational officers**.
- Runs programmes for the **organised, unorganised and rural** sectors.
- Conducts awareness camps on social security, wages, safety and women's issues.
- Has regional centres across the country.

## Why it matters to unions

Workers' education is a long-term investment. A union that explains the law to its members, and a worker who knows what the Code says, are both stronger in any negotiation. For BMS, which describes itself as a *sanskar* movement as well as a trade union, education is at the heart of its work.

## Learn more

The Board's website lists its centres, courses and publications.
